To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the testicular feminizing mutation of the androgens receptor in male rats results in increased anxiety-related behaviors and corticosterone levels following exposure to a mildly stressful situation.

1) male rats with the AR mutation Tfm show increased anxiety-related behavior in the elevated plus maze and open field, 2) Tfm males show increased c-Fos activation in the medial preoptic area and decreased activation in the dentate gyrus and posterodorsal lateral amygdala following exposure to a stressor, 3) Tfm males have an increased corticosterone response and increased c-Fos expression in the PVN following exposure to a stressful event, and

1) male rats with the Tfm mutation of the androgene receptor display elevated anxiety related behavior and corticosteroid response to mild stress, 2) testosterone influences the hypothalami-pituitary adrenal axis, anxiety related behavior and sensori-motor gating in rodents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the male hormone testosterone in the development of the brain and behavior.
the neurobiological mechanisms underlying the effects of stress on the development of psychopathology.
understanding the role of testosterone and the androgen receptor in the regulation of stress and anxiety-related behaviors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the androgen receptor plays an essential role in regulating anxiety and corticosterone responses to mild stress in male rats.
the AR is important for regulating corticosterone responses to mild stressors and that the AR plays a role in regulating the neural activation of brain areas associated with the stress response.
androgens are important modulators of the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis and anxiety in male rodents, and that this effect is mediated in part via the androgen receptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Tfm males have an enhanced corticosterone response, increased anxiety-related behavior, increased startle response, and altered c-Fos expression in response to a mild stress.
the androgen receptor is involved in mediating the response of corticosterone, anxiety-related behaviors and neural activity to a mild stress in rats.
the ARs play an important role in mediating the effects of testosterone on anxiety, corticosterone, and neural activation following mild stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the androgen receptor plays a role in regulating the stress hormone cortisone and anxiety-related behavior in male rats, and this may help explain the elevated anxiety and stress hormone response to mild stress in males with androgen insensitivity.
ARs may play an important role in regulating the HPA axis in response to mild stress in rats, and may also be important for regulating anxiety-related behaviors.
the AR plays a significant role in mediating the stress response, as well as the anxiety response, in rats.
